item.description:
Open
Eisenkot keeps saying that he doesn't meet the criteria of the Zionist parties, and he keeps mentioning the ultra-Orthodox and the Arabs. But it turns out that maybe this wasn't a mistake.

The faction within Agudat Yisrael affiliated with the Gur Hasidic dynasty, the second-largest in the party, currently has two Knesset members, Yitzhak Goldknopf and Yaakov Tesler. According to sources within the Hasidic community, they do not intend to vote against a government headed by Eisenkot.
Now tell me why. Did we give them something?
First, of course they're hoping for something, but beyond that, they want to signal to Netanyahu that his time is up.

As far as the Gerrer Rebbe, the head of Gur, is concerned, Netanyahu is finished, so they won't oppose a government headed by Eisenkot. That's one. Second, they're convinced that all of Agudat Yisrael, the Hasidic faction, will be with them. Third, they believe that ultimately even Degel HaTorah, the Lithuanian faction, will abstain, so that all the Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox are together.

Why? Because of the great anger toward Netanyahu. I have to say that I don't know about Degel HaTorah, nor do I know about the rest of Agudat Yisrael. Just yesterday, Rabbi Hirsch, spoke about the need to do everything possible to prevent the left from gaining strength. Some interpreted this to mean the political left, rather than the forces of the Sitra Achra, the "Other Side" of Jewish mysticism, the realm of impurity and evil, which is often how the word "left" is used in ultra-Orthodox discourse.

To sum up the whole story: up until now, we've said that Netanyahu's insurance policy against the swearing-in of an Eisenkot government after the elections is to reach a tie between the blocs, 54-54. That way Netanyahu can feel secure and sleep relatively peacefully at night. Now he needs to surpass the Eisenkot bloc by two seats.

כוחות צה״ל ומג״ב פעלו במהלך הלילה (ב’) במרחב הכפר ג׳אלוד שבחטיבת שומרון, לפיזור פורעים ישראלים ולהגנה על תושבי הכפר, בשעה שתואמה חזרה של משפחה פלסטינית לביתה בכפר, אותו נאלצה לנטוש לאחר מספר אירועי פשיעה לאומנית נגדה. בשל האלימות, משימת השבתם לביתם לא הושלמה.

בכפר, נכחו למעלה מ- 100 פורעים ישראלים שחסמו צירים, הבעירו צמיגים ויידו אבנים לעבר כוחות הביטחון. כמו כן, הפורעים שרפו מבנים של פלסטינים בכפר, הציתו רכבים ורכוש נוסף. 
כתוצאה מהעימותים נפצעו שלושה לוחמי מג"ב באופן קל ונגרם נזק לרכב של כוחות הביטחון.

הכוחות פעלו במקום לפיזור ההתקהלות בעזרת אמצעים לפיזור הפגנות ועצרו שני חשודים שהועברו לחקירה במשטרת מחוז ש״י. בהמשך, ייכנסו לזירה חוקרי מחוז ש״י יחד עם חוקרי הזיהוי הפלילי באבטחת כוחות צה״ל לאיסוף ממצאים, ראיות וגביית עדויות לטובת החקירה שהחלה.

מערכת הביטחון מגנה בכל תוקף כל פגיעה באנשי ביטחון במהלך מילוי תפקידם, מעשי ונדליזם ופגיעה ברכוש. 

אירועים מסוג זה מסיטים את הקשב, מערערים את היציבות ופוגעים בפעילות ההגנה והסיכול של כוחות הביטחון.

IDF Spokesperson:

IDF and Border Police forces operated overnight (Monday) in the area of the village of Jalud, in the Samaria Brigade sector, to disperse Israeli rioters and protect the village’s residents, while the coordinated return of a Palestinian family to its home in the village was underway. The family had been forced to leave its home following several incidents of nationalist-motivated crime against them. Due to the violence, the mission to return the family to its home was not completed.

More than 100 Israeli rioters were present in the village. They blocked roads, burned tires, and threw stones at security forces. The rioters also burned Palestinian structures in the village and set fire to vehicles and other property.

Three Border Police officers were lightly injured in the clashes, and a security forces vehicle was damaged.

The forces acted to disperse the gathering using riot-control measures and arrested two suspects, who were transferred for questioning by the Judea and Samaria District Police. Later, Judea and Samaria District investigators, together with forensic investigators and under IDF protection, will enter the scene to collect findings and evidence and take statements as part of the investigation that has been opened.

The security establishment strongly condemns any harm to security personnel while carrying out their duties, as well as acts of vandalism and damage to property.

Incidents of this kind divert attention, undermine stability, and impair the security forces’ defensive and counterterrorism operations.
